questions.question: What is the maximum number of interfaces that can be aggregated with EtherChannel and PAgP?
questions.explanation: PAgP EtherChannel can bundle up to eight active interfaces.

correct.explanation: EtherChannel with PAgP supports up to 8 active links in a port channel on Cisco platforms.

incorrect.explanation: Two links can bundle but the maximum with PAgP is 8, not 2.
incorrect.whatItDoes: 2 interfaces points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", 8 interfaces satisfies what this question tests — 2 interfaces does not.

incorrect.explanation: 16 exceeds the PAgP EtherChannel limit — Cisco caps at 8 member interfaces.
incorrect.whatItDoes: 16 interfaces points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", 8 interfaces satisfies what this question tests — 16 interfaces does not.

incorrect.explanation: Four links can aggregate but the exam maximum for PAgP EtherChannel is 8.
incorrect.whatItDoes: 4 interfaces points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", 8 interfaces satisfies what this question tests — 4 interfaces does not.

answerReview.examTip: PAgP/LACP EtherChannel max = 8 links (same speed/duplex, same VLAN settings).

questions.question: Which is a true statement about EtherChannel?
choices: EtherChannel works with 802.1Q to block the redundant links.
EtherChannel can aggregate multiple links with varying speed.
EtherChannel can aggregate interfaces across multiple stand- alone switches.
When configured, EtherChannel acts as a single layer 2 connection.
questions.explanation: EtherChannel acts as one logical Layer 2 link.

correct.explanation: EtherChannel bundles physical links into one logical L2 connection — STP sees one link, no blocking.

incorrect.explanation: EtherChannel prevents blocking by combining links — 802.1Q trunking is separate from link aggregation.
incorrect.whatItDoes: EtherChannel works with 802.1Q to block the redundant links. expects VLAN tags on a link that should behave as access-only in this stem.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", When configured, EtherChannel acts as a single layer 2 connection. satisfies what this question tests — EtherChannel works with 802.1Q to block the redundant links. does not.

incorrect.explanation: All bundled ports must match speed and duplex — varying speed is not supported.
incorrect.whatItDoes: EtherChannel can aggregate multiple links with varying speed. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", When configured, EtherChannel acts as a single layer 2 connection. satisfies what this question tests — EtherChannel can aggregate multiple links with varying speed. does not.

incorrect.explanation: EtherChannel bundles ports on the same switch pair — cross-chassis needs vPC/VSS/StackWise.
incorrect.whatItDoes: EtherChannel can aggregate interfaces across multiple stand- alone switches. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", When configured, EtherChannel acts as a single layer 2 connection. satisfies what this question tests — EtherChannel can aggregate interfaces across multiple stand- alone switches. does not.

answerReview.examTip: EtherChannel = single logical link → STP sees one path, no blocking; all ports must match speed/duplex/VLAN.

questions.question: You have a switch with 2 gigabit interface ports and 48 FastEthernet ports and are using PAgP. What is the highest bandwidth you can achieve?
questions.explanation: Links in an EtherChannel must use the same speed and duplex.

correct.explanation: EtherChannel members must match speed and duplex — only the two gigabit ports can bundle, giving 2 Gb/s aggregate with PAgP.

incorrect.explanation: You cannot mix FastEthernet and Gigabit in one channel group — 2.2 Gb/s is not achievable with mismatched port speeds.
incorrect.whatItDoes: 2.2 Gb/s points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", 2 Gb/s satisfies what this question tests — 2.2 Gb/s does not.

incorrect.explanation: 400 Mb/s would require bundling FastEthernet ports only — the question asks for highest bandwidth using PAgP across available ports.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Under-counting by ignoring the gigabit pair
incorrect.whatItDoes: 400 Mb/s points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", 2 Gb/s satisfies what this question tests — 400 Mb/s does not.

incorrect.explanation: 2.6 Gb/s implies mixing link speeds — EtherChannel requires homogeneous speed/duplex on all members.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Adding incompatible port speeds into one bundle
incorrect.whatItDoes: 2.6 Gb/s points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", 2 Gb/s satisfies what this question tests — 2.6 Gb/s does not.

answerReview.examTip: EtherChannel rule: same speed + duplex on every member — no mixing FE and GE.

questions.question: Which aggregation protocol is an IEEE standard?
questions.explanation: LACP is the IEEE 802.3ad link aggregation standard.

correct.explanation: LACP (802.3ad) is the IEEE standard link aggregation protocol — PAgP is Cisco proprietary.

incorrect.explanation: 802.1Q is VLAN trunk encapsulation — not a link aggregation negotiation protocol.
incorrect.whatItDoes: 802.1Q expects VLAN tags on a link that should behave as access-only in this stem.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", LACP satisfies what this question tests — 802.1Q does not.

incorrect.explanation: PAgP is Cisco proprietary — the IEEE standard for EtherChannel negotiation is LACP (802.3ad).
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Selecting PAgP as the IEEE standard
incorrect.whatItDoes: PAgP points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", LACP satisfies what this question tests — PAgP does not.

incorrect.explanation: 802.1X is port-based network access control — unrelated to bundling physical links.
incorrect.whatItDoes: 802.1X points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", LACP satisfies what this question tests — 802.1X does not.

answerReview.examTip: IEEE EtherChannel protocol → LACP (802.3ad); Cisco-only → PAgP.

questions.question: You need to form an EtherChannel between a VMware ESXi host and the switch. Which negotiation protocol will you choose?
questions.explanation: Use LACP for non-Cisco link aggregation compatibility.

correct.explanation: LACP (802.3ad) is the IEEE standard — VMware ESXi and third-party hosts require LACP, not Cisco PAgP.

incorrect.explanation: "EtherChannel" is the feature name, not a negotiation protocol — you must pick LACP or PAgP explicitly.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Naming the feature instead of the negotiation protocol
incorrect.whatItDoes: EtherChannel points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", LACP satisfies what this question tests — EtherChannel does not.

incorrect.explanation: "Channel Group" describes the interface bundle — it is not the inter-vendor negotiation protocol.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Channel Group points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", LACP satisfies what this question tests — Channel Group does not.

incorrect.explanation: PAgP is Cisco-proprietary — non-Cisco ESXi hosts will not negotiate PAgP successfully.
incorrect.whatItDoes: PAgP points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", LACP satisfies what this question tests — PAgP does not.

answerReview.examTip: Non-Cisco link aggregation → LACP. Cisco-to-Cisco can use PAgP or LACP.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of interfaces that can be aggregated with EtherChannel and LACP?
questions.explanation: LACP can aggregate up to 16 interfaces, with eight active and others standby.

correct.explanation: LACP supports up to 16 interfaces per bundle (8 active + 8 hot-standby).

incorrect.explanation: 2 interfaces is too few — LACP supports 8 active (16 total with standby).
incorrect.whatItDoes: 2 interfaces points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", 16 interfaces satisfies what this question tests — 2 interfaces does not.

incorrect.explanation: 8 is the active maximum — LACP actually supports 16 (8 active + 8 standby).
incorrect.whatItDoes: 8 interfaces points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", 16 interfaces satisfies what this question tests — 8 interfaces does not.

incorrect.explanation: 4 interfaces is too low — EtherChannel/LACP can do up to 16.
incorrect.whatItDoes: 4 interfaces points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", 16 interfaces satisfies what this question tests — 4 interfaces does not.

answerReview.examTip: LACP: 8 active + 8 standby = 16 total | PAgP: up to 8 ports per bundle.

questions.question: Which mode forces the aggregation of links without the use of a control protocol?
questions.explanation: on mode forms an unconditional port channel without LACP or PAgP.

correct.explanation: Channel-group mode on forces the bundle without LACP or PAgP — both sides must match on.

incorrect.explanation: LACP uses active/passive negotiation — on mode bypasses LACP entirely.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Calling forced bundle LACP off mode
incorrect.whatItDoes: LACP off mode points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", On mode satisfies what this question tests — LACP off mode does not.

incorrect.explanation: PAgP uses desirable/auto — on mode does not use PAgP at all.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Labeling on mode as PAgP off
incorrect.whatItDoes: PAgP off mode points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", On mode satisfies what this question tests — PAgP off mode does not.

incorrect.explanation: 802.3ad is LACP — on mode forms an unconditional static port-channel without control protocol.
incorrect.whatItDoes: 802.3ad mode points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", On mode satisfies what this question tests — 802.3ad mode does not.

answerReview.examTip: No negotiation protocol → channel-group <n> mode on on both ends.

questions.question: Which is a correct statement about aggregating ports together?
choices: The term EtherChannel is a Cisco proprietary term for port channeling.
PAgP can be used with non-Cisco products.
LACP can only be used with other Cisco switches.
PAgP can bundle several different links with varying speeds and duplexes together.
questions.explanation: EtherChannel is a Cisco-centric term for port channeling.

correct.explanation: EtherChannel is Cisco's proprietary term for port-channel / link aggregation technology.

incorrect.explanation: PAgP is Cisco-proprietary — it does not work with non-Cisco; use LACP for multi-vendor.
incorrect.whatItDoes: PAgP can be used with non-Cisco products. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", The term EtherChannel is a Cisco proprietary term for port channeling. satisfies what this question tests — PAgP can be used with non-Cisco products. does not.

incorrect.explanation: LACP (802.3ad) is the open standard — works with any vendor, not Cisco-only.
incorrect.whatItDoes: LACP can only be used with other Cisco switches. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", The term EtherChannel is a Cisco proprietary term for port channeling. satisfies what this question tests — LACP can only be used with other Cisco switches. does not.

incorrect.explanation: PAgP requires matching speed/duplex on all ports — no mixed-speed bundling.
incorrect.whatItDoes: PAgP can bundle several different links with varying speeds and duplexes together. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", The term EtherChannel is a Cisco proprietary term for port channeling. satisfies what this question tests — PAgP can bundle several different links with varying speeds and duplexes together. does not.

answerReview.examTip: EtherChannel = Cisco branding | PAgP = Cisco protocol | LACP = IEEE 802.3ad open standard.

questions.question: Which negotiation protocol is a Cisco proprietary standard?

correct.explanation: PAgP (Port Aggregation Protocol) is Cisco proprietary — LACP (802.3ad) is the open standard.

incorrect.explanation: LACP (802.3ad) is IEEE open standard — Cisco proprietary negotiation is PAgP.
incorrect.whatItDoes: LACP points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", PAgP satisfies what this question tests — LACP does not.

incorrect.explanation: 802.1Q is VLAN trunk tagging — link bundling negotiation is PAgP or LACP.
incorrect.whatItDoes: 802.1Q expects VLAN tags on a link that should behave as access-only in this stem.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", PAgP satisfies what this question tests — 802.1Q does not.

incorrect.explanation: 802.1ab is LLDP neighbor discovery — not EtherChannel negotiation.
incorrect.whatItDoes: 802.1ab points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", PAgP satisfies what this question tests — 802.1ab does not.

answerReview.examTip: Cisco-only bundling → PAgP ( desirable/auto); multi-vendor → LACP (active/passive).

questions.question: How often does PAgP send messages to control the status of the links in the bundle?
questions.explanation: PAgP sends control messages every 30 seconds.

correct.explanation: PAgP sends control messages every 30 seconds to maintain bundle status.

incorrect.explanation: 60 seconds is incorrect — PAgP interval is 30 seconds.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Every 60 seconds states a MAC aging timer or timeout value that may not match the default or configured setting.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", Every 30 seconds satisfies what this question tests — Every 60 seconds does not.

incorrect.explanation: 90 seconds is not the PAgP timer — it's 30 seconds.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Every 90 seconds states a MAC aging timer or timeout value that may not match the default or configured setting.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", Every 30 seconds satisfies what this question tests — Every 90 seconds does not.

incorrect.explanation: 120 seconds is far too slow — PAgP uses 30-second messages.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Every 120 seconds states a MAC aging timer or timeout value that may not match the default or configured setting.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", Every 30 seconds satisfies what this question tests — Every 120 seconds does not.

questions.question: You want to configure two switches so that LACP is used between the switches. Which mode should you use on both sides to force LACP?
questions.explanation: LACP active mode actively starts negotiation.

correct.explanation: LACP requires at least one side in active mode to start negotiation — active on both sides guarantees LACP forms.

incorrect.explanation: Passive on both sides waits forever — neither side initiates LACP. You need active on at least one side (both active is fine).
incorrect.whatItDoes: Passive mode on both sides points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", Active mode on both sides satisfies what this question tests — Passive mode on both sides does not.

incorrect.explanation: Auto is PAgP terminology, not LACP. This stem asks specifically for LACP between switches.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Auto mode on both sides points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", Active mode on both sides satisfies what this question tests — Auto mode on both sides does not.

incorrect.explanation: Desirable is also PAgP — not IEEE 802.3ad LACP. Use channel-group mode active/passive for LACP.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Selecting Cisco PAgP modes on an LACP question
incorrect.whatItDoes: Desirable mode on both sides points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", Active mode on both sides satisfies what this question tests — Desirable mode on both sides does not.

answerReview.examTip: LACP = active/passive. PAgP = desirable/auto. Passive + passive never forms a bundle.

questions.question: What is the effect of configuring a port channel with one side set to passive mode and the other side set to active mode?
choices: The channel group will use PAgP.
The channel group will not be formed.
The channel group will use LACP.
The channel group will use EtherChannel.
questions.explanation: Passive plus active forms an LACP channel.

correct.explanation: Passive + active on both sides forms an LACP (802.3ad) EtherChannel — passive waits, active initiates.

incorrect.explanation: PAgP uses desirable/auto keywords — LACP uses active/passive. This pairing is LACP, not PAgP.
incorrect.whatItDoes: The channel group will use PAgP. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", The channel group will use LACP. satisfies what this question tests — The channel group will use PAgP. does not.

incorrect.explanation: Passive + active is a valid LACP combination — passive + passive would fail to negotiate.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Believing active/passive cannot form a channel
incorrect.whatItDoes: The channel group will not be formed. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", The channel group will use LACP. satisfies what this question tests — The channel group will not be formed. does not.

incorrect.explanation: EtherChannel is the feature name — the question asks which protocol negotiates; LACP (802.3ad) is the answer for active/passive.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Answering generic EtherChannel when LACP protocol is required
incorrect.whatItDoes: The channel group will use EtherChannel. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", The channel group will use LACP. satisfies what this question tests — The channel group will use EtherChannel. does not.

answerReview.examTip: LACP: active/passive or active/active. PAgP: desirable/auto.

questions.question: Which command is used to verify the negotiation protocol for a port channel?
questions.explanation: show etherchannel verifies EtherChannel information and negotiated protocol.

correct.explanation: show etherchannel displays protocol (LACP/PAgP), port state, and bundle summary.

incorrect.explanation: show port-channel is incomplete — use show etherchannel summary or show etherchannel.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch#show port-channel points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", Switch#show etherchannel satisfies what this question tests — Switch#show port-channel does not.

incorrect.explanation: show interface shows L1/L2 detail — not the EtherChannel negotiation protocol.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch#show interface points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", Switch#show etherchannel satisfies what this question tests — Switch#show interface does not.

incorrect.explanation: show run shows config text — show etherchannel gives live status.
incorrect.whatItDoes: Switch#show run is a verification command that inspects a different table or feature than the stem asks about.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: Verification command (etherchannel): Switch#show etherchannel inspects the right table or state — Switch#show run shows unrelated information.

answerReview.examTip: EtherChannel verify: show etherchannel summary (protocol + port flags) | show etherchannel detail for timers.

questions.question: What is the effect of configuring a port channel with one side set to passive mode and the other side set to passive mode?
choices: The channel group will use PAgP.
The channel group will not be formed.
The channel group will use LACP.
An unconditional port channel will be formed.
questions.explanation: Passive plus passive does not form LACP because neither side initiates.

correct.explanation: LACP passive on both sides means neither initiates — no PDUs are exchanged, so the port channel never forms.

incorrect.explanation: PAgP is a different protocol family — this scenario describes LACP passive/passive, not PAgP negotiation.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Switching to PAgP when LACP modes are specified
incorrect.whatItDoes: The channel group will use PAgP. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", The channel group will not be formed. satisfies what this question tests — The channel group will use PAgP. does not.

incorrect.explanation: The channel does not form at all — passive/passive produces no LACP PDUs, so there is no bundle to "use LACP" on.
incorrect.whatItDoes: The channel group will use LACP. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", The channel group will not be formed. satisfies what this question tests — The channel group will use LACP. does not.

incorrect.explanation: mode on forces a channel without negotiation — passive/passive is not unconditional and will not form.
incorrect.whatItDoes: An unconditional port channel will be formed. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", The channel group will not be formed. satisfies what this question tests — An unconditional port channel will be formed. does not.

answerReview.examTip: LACP passive + passive = no channel. Need active on at least one side.

questions.question: What is the effect of configuring a port channel with one side set to on mode and the other side set to on mode?
choices: The channel group will use PAgP.
The channel group will not be formed.
The channel group will use LACP.
An unconditional port channel will be formed.
questions.explanation: On plus on forms an unconditional port channel.

correct.explanation: When both sides use mode on, IOS forms an unconditional port-channel without LACP or PAgP packets.

incorrect.explanation: PAgP requires desirable/auto modes — dual on does not send PAgP hellos.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Expecting PAgP with both sides in on mode
incorrect.whatItDoes: The channel group will use PAgP. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", An unconditional port channel will be formed. satisfies what this question tests — The channel group will use PAgP. does not.

incorrect.explanation: Matching on mode on both switches forms the bundle — mismatched modes fail, not matching on/on.
incorrect.whatItDoes: The channel group will not be formed. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", An unconditional port channel will be formed. satisfies what this question tests — The channel group will not be formed. does not.

incorrect.explanation: LACP requires active/passive — on/on is static bundling without LACP.
incorrect.misconceptionTested: Expecting LACP when both sides are on
incorrect.whatItDoes: The channel group will use LACP. points to a related idea, but not the specific behavior or value required for etherchannel.
incorrect.whyWrongHere: For "etherchannel", An unconditional port channel will be formed. satisfies what this question tests — The channel group will use LACP. does not.

answerReview.examTip: Both ends mode on → static port-channel (no LACP/PAgP).
